plugin_desc: SNMP monitoring template for DCN switch. It reports uptime, CPU utilization, memory utilization, temperature, fan, power supply status, and interface traffic (enterprise PEN 6339).
name: Switch

metrics.name: device_cpu_usage
metrics.description: This metric reports the CPU utilization of the DCN switch control plane (DCN-MIB switchCpuUsage, a direct percent value from a scalar GET with instance .0), normalized to 0-100. Sustained high CPU usage can indicate control-plane overload, routing instability, or attack traffic, and may lead to slow management response or packet processing delays.

metrics.name: device_memory_total
metrics.description: This metric reports the total size in bytes of the DCN switch system memory (DCN-MIB switchMemorySize, a scalar GET with instance .0, reported directly in bytes). Together with the used bytes it determines overall memory utilization.

metrics.name: device_memory_used
metrics.description: This metric reports the number of bytes currently in use by the DCN switch system memory (DCN-MIB switchMemoryBusy, a scalar GET with instance .0, reported directly in bytes). It helps administrators understand absolute memory consumption and identify when the device is under memory pressure.

metrics.name: device_memory_usage
metrics.description: This metric reports overall memory utilization of the DCN switch, computed as used / total * 100. High memory usage may indicate memory leaks, oversized routing/MAC/ARP tables, or insufficient capacity, and can cause instability or failed allocations.

metrics.name: device_temperature_celsius
metrics.description: This metric reports the chassis temperature of the DCN switch (DCN-MIB switchTemperature), in degrees Celsius from a scalar GET with instance .0. Abnormally high temperatures may indicate fan failure, blocked airflow, or excessive ambient heat, and can trigger thermal protection or hardware damage if left unaddressed.

metrics.name: device_fan_state
metrics.description: This metric reports the operational state of each DCN cooling fan (DCN-MIB sysFanStatus). The native enum is inverted (normal=0, abnormal=1) and is normalized to the unified convention where 1 means normal and any other value indicates an abnormal/fault state. A non-normal state indicates a cooling fault that can quickly lead to overheating and should be investigated immediately.

metrics.name: device_fan_speed
metrics.description: This metric reports the DCN fan speed grade (DCN-MIB sysFanSpeed): none(0), low(1), medium-low(2), medium(3), medium-high(4), high(5). It is a discrete enum, not RPM.

metrics.name: device_psu_state
metrics.description: This metric reports the operational state of each DCN power supply unit (DCN-MIB sysPowerStatus: native normal(0)/abnormal(1)/na(2)). The native enum is inverted (normal=0) and is normalized to the unified convention where 1 means normal and any other value (including na) indicates an abnormal/unavailable state. sysPowerState (sysPowerInstalled(1)/sysPowerNotInstalled(0)) is collected alongside as device_psu_present. A non-normal state signals a power redundancy or hardware fault and must be remediated promptly.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCInOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of bytes received over the past 5 minutes, measured in bytes per second, from the 64-bit IF-MIB ifHCInOctets counter (ifXTable). The 64-bit counter avoids the rapid wrap of the 32-bit ifInOctets on high-speed switch ports, keeping the rate accurate.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCOutOctets
metrics.description: This metric calculates the average rate of bytes sent over the past 5 minutes, measured in bytes per second, from the 64-bit IF-MIB ifHCOutOctets counter (ifXTable). The 64-bit counter avoids the rapid wrap of the 32-bit ifOutOctets on high-speed switch ports, keeping the rate accurate.

metrics.name: snmp_uptime
metrics.description: This metric indicates the uptime of the device since the last restart. By monitoring the uptime, network administrators can understand the stability and reliability of the device and identify potential reboot or failure issues.
